title: MV Images (like busts) in menu windows - Javascript help

posts.author: FriKitty
posts.body:
Hello everyone! I start with the warning:
I am a noob at Javascript
. I barely know what I'm doing.
I have been making a plugin to customize my menus (RPG Maker MV), and while my code is probably shoddy and does stupid things, it's working so far! I am only moving things around and sometimes hiding parts I don't need. So far so good. But how do I go about adding images to menus? I'm specifically thinking about a
bust for each actor that you could see in their status window
.
I tried to investigate other plugins that do this, like Galv's and SRD's bust plugins, but unlike other times I looked at their code, this time around I have no idea how adding pictures that aren't faces or icons remotely work T_T And it's been very frustrating. I also tried reading the seemingly related core scripts and I'm still very confused.
Could someone be so kind (and... patient) to explain how I should add an image that isn't used in the Database for anything else? Having in mind that my plugin process has been just copying and pasting whatever I could read in the core scripts, and tinkering with it until it looks good? Maybe I just need to come back next weekend with a clearer mind, but some help would be very appreciated @_@
It would also be awesome to learn how to implement
plugin commands
, with the idea of changing these busts corresponding to each character depending on the story (I'm also going to change their sprites and faces, so...). However, that's a question for later, and I should start with the images haha.
Thank you very much! Regardless of how much help I can get here, I think I shall try again next weekend x)

My personal, somewhat professional advice, is to do some proper tutorials. I like w3schools, starting with the Statements chapter, but there are many options if you Google it (and there are other things like YouTube classes and books and such).
It's less satisfying than moving stuff around in existing code and seeing what happens right away, but you'll actually understand what you're doing. And you'll start to understand the code that you're reading, so you'll be able to figure out answers by reading it.
I haven't looked at SRD's, but Galv's bust plugin is too advanced to hack around and figure stuff out that way - he creates an entire new sprite class for his bust images, with the associated methods.
Briefly, to draw an image that isn't a predefined type (e.g. face, icon, character...) you'd use the Bitmap.blt() function on the contents of a window.

Well, you don't show anything you tried so I can't really help just based off "nothing is working"
But if you look up any of the existing draw functions, like
Window_Base.prototype.drawFace
, you can see the example of how it loads the desired image file from disk, gets the coordinates to draw (which in your case would be the entire dimensions of the bust), then uses blt() on the window's contents at the bottom.

posts.body:
FriKitty said:
Then there's all the pw, ph, sx and sy that I don't understand much.
Click to expand...
Which parts don't you understand? They're all described above the function definition in the code that you quoted.
FriKitty said:
JavaScript:
@method blt
 * @param {Bitmap} source The bitmap to draw
 * @param {Number} sx The x coordinate in the source
 * @param {Number} sy The y coordinate in the source
 * @param {Number} sw The width of the source image
 * @param {Number} sh The height of the source image
 * @param {Number} dx The x coordinate in the destination
 * @param {Number} dy The y coordinate in the destination
 * @param {Number} [dw=sw] The width to draw the image in the destination
 * @param {Number} [dh=sh] The height to draw the image in the destination
 */
Click to expand...
FriKitty said:
They are all used for the next function,
this.contents.blt()
, (why contents?).
Click to expand...
Because contents is the bitmap property of a window that actually displays what you see.
Code:
/**
 * The bitmap used for the window contents.
 *
 * @property contents
 * @type Bitmap
 */
Object.defineProperty(Window.prototype, 'contents', {
    get: function() {
        return this._windowContentsSprite.bitmap;
    },
    set: function(value) {
        this._windowContentsSprite.bitmap = value;
    },
    configurable: true
});
FriKitty said:
Well, that explains some, sx and sy. But what is pw and ph? Width and height of... what?
Click to expand...
The names of variables passed as arguments have nothing to do with how those parameters are named in the actual function.
JavaScript Function Study Path
Learn Functions in the Right Order.
www.w3schools.com
It makes no difference whether this example uses 4, 3, declares variables named apple, orange, or whatever else. They're still used inside the function in the order they were input.
FriKitty said:
Aren't many parameters missing from drawIcon?
Click to expand...
Yes, but if the code checks for them to exist and doesn't try to reference them when they're not, then that doesn't matter. It's moderately common to have functions with optional arguments.
FriKitty said:
So that's where I'm at. What am I supposed to do here?
Click to expand...
Load an image, then put it in your window.
Your code has a number of problems. For one, why on Earth are you making up your own bltImage() function? Especially when it's a direct copy of the existing blt() function. What's the point of that?
The image doesn't work because you're calling
this.bltImage()
- you saw in the example you looked at that the bitmap to receive the image was
this.contents
so why would you write yours as just
this
, which is a Window_Status object? That has no visual properties to be seen.
As a side note, you should not have non-URL-compliant characters in your filenames (such as the space in "Busto Fendi"). That can cause the files to not load and crash your game when the project is deployed.
